name: Network type, metered and constrained flags
plain: Reads whether the phone is on Wi-Fi, cellular or VPN, and if the connection is metered.
meaning: Tells whether the person is at home or out, and whether data saving is on.

android.note: Transports: WIFI, CELLULAR, ETHERNET, VPN, BLUETOOTH

ios.api_surface: Interface types: wifi, cellular, wiredEthernet, other

limits.headline: Can tell if you are on Wi-Fi, cellular or VPN, and if data is metered
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app loads or before it downloads something big
can: Check if the phone uses Wi-Fi, cellular, Ethernet, VPN or Bluetooth
Check if the connection is metered or limited
Wait for Wi-Fi before big downloads
cannot: See the network's name without more permission
See what you send or receive
limits.differs: Android needs a normal permission granted at install. iPhone needs none.

story.what_it_is: An app can see if you are on Wi-Fi, cellular or a VPN, and whether data saving is on.

marketing.name: Connectivity status
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps check what network you are on so they can save your data.

marketing.name: Network path monitor
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps watch the connection type and whether it is expensive or constrained.

story.for_you: You do not see it. You notice that a podcast app waits for Wi-Fi to download, or a video drops to a lower quality on cellular. It also tells an app whether you are at home or out.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to save your data, lower video quality, and defer big downloads. It is a low risk signal. Over time it shows when you are at home, at work or on the move.

use_cases.example: A streaming app drops video quality on cellular to protect your data plan.
A music app only downloads your playlists when you are on Wi-Fi.
A game waits for Wi-Fi before it downloads a big update.
A live stream app lowers its picture when your signal gets weak.
A cloud photo backup runs only on Wi-Fi or when plugged in.
A tracker logs when you switch from home Wi-Fi to cellular to learn your day.

story.android_note: Android reads network type, metered and VPN flags with the normal network state permission.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps see whether a connection is expensive or constrained, which covers cellular and Low Data Mode.
